about: The Election Almanac for the 2026 US midterms: which election story shapes will surge in election week, forecast before the polls open and scored afterwards. Probabilities start from October's tellings, the motifs' notes and the 2020, 2022 and 2024 pattern.

rules.name: The window
rules.text: Tellings dated Tuesday Nov 3 to Monday Nov 9, 2026, seven days, from every kind of teller: shows, posts retold online, fact-checks and voters.

rules.name: Which day
rules.text: A telling's day is the day the motif index records for it. A show's is the day its episode was published, in UTC, so an episode out after 7 PM Eastern on a Monday counts as Tuesday.

rules.name: The count
rules.text: Counted on Tuesday Nov 17 from the public index, the motifs and claims the site shows. The window and the baseline week are both counted that day, from the same index.

rules.name: A surge
rules.text: A motif surges if its share of all the window's tellings is at least twice its share of all tellings in the baseline week, Oct 20-26, and it has at least 3 tellings in the window. Shares, not counts, because how much the site reads swings from week to week.

rules.name: Why Oct 20-26
rules.text: Until Oct 20 our show transcripts were thin: they caught about 3 characters a second of speech, against about 16 since a fix that day, so the shows gave about 7 claims an episode before and about 24 after. Shares from early October would mix thin weeks with full ones, and every show-told motif would look like it surged. So the baseline is the one full week before the vote, Oct 20-26, read the same way as the window will be. That week had its own news (Brazil's runoff among it), which a single week can't average out.

rules.name: The score
rules.text: The Brier score: the mean, over the motifs, of (forecast probability - outcome) squared, where the outcome is 1 for a surge and 0 for none. Lower is better; 0 is perfect.

rules.name: The yardstick
rules.text: A reference forecaster gives every motif the same 0.148: the share of election motifs whose weekly share doubled, with at least 3 tellings, in the week of Oct 13 against the weeks before it (27 motif-weeks). That comparison is taken before the transcript fix on both sides; the week of Oct 20 against the weeks before is left out, because the fix alone made show-told motifs look like they surged (it gave 0.271 with it in). Skill = 1 - our Brier / the reference's Brier. Above 0 beats the yardstick; below 0 loses to it.

rules.name: Side calls
rules.text: Among motifs with at least 3 show tellings in the window, the lead side is the side (left, center or right) whose shows told it at the highest rate: its tellings there over all that side's show tellings in the window. A call naming two sides is a hit if either leads. Calls of both sides, posts or fact-checks name no single show side, so they are shown but not scored. A call that depends on who wins the House is scored on the branch that happened, as AP calls it. The yardstick is persistence: each motif's lead side in the baseline week, by the same rule.

rules.name: Answer calls
rules.text: Each is a hit or a miss, shown with its probability. A call about a motif that isn't public on the count day is not scored.

rules.name: The seal
rules.text: Before Nov 3, 00:00 Eastern, the forecast is frozen: its SHA-256 fingerprint is published here, and the page refuses to score a forecast whose fingerprint no longer matches. It is never edited afterwards, and it is scored win or lose.

forecasts.name: Red mirage
forecasts.why: Late counts in CA/AZ/NV etc. make the slow count itself the story; already pre-bunked on the left (Oct 24).

forecasts.name: Sore loser
forecasts.why: Losers who will not concede; October tellings were mostly Brazil (Flavio Bolsonaro, Oct 26).

forecasts.name: Rigged election
forecasts.lead_side: right if D; left if R
forecasts.why: Fraud claims follow the loss; checkers check many (13 of 42 October tellings were checks).

forecasts.name: Voter fraud
forecasts.why: Noncitizen-voting claims carry on through the count (DOJ suits in CA).

forecasts.name: Voter suppression
forecasts.why: Election-day lines, ID rules, federal agents near polls; posts tell it most (11 of 32 in October).

forecasts.name: Ballot security
forecasts.why: Armed guards or federal agents near the vote become the story on the day.

forecasts.name: Black box voting
forecasts.why: Machine glitches on the day become rigged-machine claims (NewsGuard, Cook County, Oct 26).

forecasts.name: Friend on the inside
forecasts.why: Viral 'my friend is a poll manager' warnings are an election-day perennial.

forecasts.name: Solution in search of a problem
forecasts.why: Follows Voter fraud as its counter.

forecasts.name: Mail in fraud
forecasts.why: Late-arriving mail ballots counted after the day.

forecasts.name: Election meddling
forecasts.why: Foreign interference reports (fake videos, bomb threats) on the day.

forecasts.name: Intimidation
forecasts.why: Intimidation at polls and of election officials.

forecasts.name: They're going to steal it
forecasts.why: A pre-vote motif: peaks before Nov 3, then turns into Rigged election or fades.

forecasts.name: Importing voters
forecasts.why: Pre-vote immigration framing; results crowd it out.

forecasts.name: Polls are inaccurate
forecasts.lead_side: the side that beat its polls
forecasts.why: Results are read against the polls whichever way they miss.

forecasts.name: Shy Tory
forecasts.why: Only if Republicans beat their polls.

forecasts.name: Polls are manipulated
forecasts.why: Already flashed Oct 21-23 (fake Wedgwood polls); less to say after the count.

forecasts.name: They're losing, actually!
forecasts.why: A pre-vote cope motif; the count settles it.

forecasts.name: The markets know
forecasts.why: Prediction markets get credited or blamed after the count, as in 2024.

forecasts.name: Midterm curse
forecasts.why: If the president's party loses seats, as it usually does, the curse explains it.

forecasts.name: Referendum on the president
forecasts.why: The result read as a verdict on Trump.

forecasts.name: Dead weight president
forecasts.why: If Republicans lose, he dragged them down.

forecasts.name: Blue Texas
forecasts.why: Texas (Tallarico v. Paxton) settles the prophecy either way.

forecasts.name: Political party surge
forecasts.why: Wave talk after the result, from a high October base.

forecasts.name: Enthusiasm gap
forecasts.why: Turnout post-mortems.

forecasts.name: Big Mo
forecasts.why: Momentum talk ends with the vote.

forecasts.name: War for votes
forecasts.why: A strike timed before the vote; falls after Nov 3 if none comes.

forecasts.name: After the election
forecasts.why: Its mirror: 'now that the vote is over, they will...'

forecasts.name: I voted
forecasts.why: 'I voted' posts on the day, if the posts pipeline keeps them as claims.

forecasts.name: Too big to rig
forecasts.why: Turnout exhortation peaks Nov 1-3; only Nov 3 is in the window.

answer_calls.call: If Voter fraud has at least 3 tellings in the window, its counter, Solution in search of a problem, has at least 2, and most of its show tellings come from center or left shows.
Voter fraud and Voter suppression both have at least 3 tellings in the window; right shows lead Voter fraud, and left shows or posts lead Voter suppression.
Pre-bunking: Red mirage is told on or before the first window day that Ballot dump is told.
After the election takes a bigger share of the window's tellings than War for votes: the reverse of the baseline week, Oct 20-26, when it was 5 to 12.
The mirror pair is told from opposite sides in the window: right shows lead Importing voters, and left shows or posts lead Voter suppression.
